risks.title: CGNK orchestration may add context and complexity without creating architecture-only successes
risks.signal: Paired essential workloads show no repeatable CGNK_ONLY chains against Direct Cheap, or CGNK failures arise from retrieval, state mismatch, or protocol overhead.
risks.response: Keep Direct Cheap as a first-class baseline, report necessity per workload family, require frozen paired evidence before reopening routing research, and do not implement Router or Multi-Agent from development-only results.

risks.title: Persistent Persona could drift, fabricate social history, overpersonalize, or bypass public-write authority
risks.signal: Identity changes without approval, episodes or commitments lack receipts, sensitive traits are inferred, unrelated history appears in public context, or Persona acts around Community/Promotion approval.
risks.response: The formal 100-episode replay recorded zero identity drift, hallucination, overpersonalization, sensitive inference, or unapproved writes. Retain immutable identity, evidence references, explicit commitments, localized relationship context, advisory-only sandboxing, exact-hash approval, and require independent human calibration before broader social use.

risks.title: Community engagement could become spam, violate platform rules, or publish without informed approval
risks.signal: A reply has low standalone value, unsupported project claims, hidden affiliation, unknown community rules, duplicate targeting, or executes without APPROVED_TO_REPLY bound to its exact revision.
risks.response: Evaluate policy before relevance, prefer precision over recall, separate engage/mention/link decisions, require claim grounding and disclosure, keep EXTERNAL_WRITE candidate-only, bind exact-hash approval, enforce idempotency and low rate limits, and suppress communities after moderation events.

risks.title: Promotion publishing could leak private evidence or bypass human authorization
risks.signal: Drafts contain local paths, unsupported claims, secrets, or an external adapter executes without an approval that binds exact content, media, and platform hashes.
risks.response: Project only explicit public-safe evidence, validate every draft against the claim ledger, keep DRAFT_ONLY default, resolve credentials locally, require exact-hash publish approval, and make EXTERNAL_WRITE proposal-only for Self-Growth.

risks.title: Compatibility runtime remains much larger than the new MVP substrate
risks.signal: New work keeps extending run_local_pipeline_impl, formal delivery, or old planning contracts instead of the CapabilityTree substrate.
risks.response: Treat the compatibility stack as migration material only and require the product direction gate for architecture changes.

risks.title: Multiple planning and graph abstractions may compete for authority
risks.signal: WorkNode, ProviderJob, decomposition tree, module flow, or planning proposal acts as a project-level source of truth beside CapabilityTree and ExecutionDAG.
risks.response: CapabilityTree is composition truth and ExecutionDAG is execution truth; other structures must be adapters or compatibility data.

risks.title: Target architecture is not yet wired into the default runtime
risks.signal: The repository describes CapabilityTree and ExecutionDAG, but real project execution still enters the compatibility pipeline.
risks.response: Keep the validated isolated route separate until an explicit migration increment replaces compatibility entrypoints.

risks.title: Executor interfaces remain fragmented
risks.signal: Provider, local model, search, script, browser, and test execution use unrelated request and result semantics.
risks.response: Continue adapting remaining executor kinds behind Block execution; the local, test, and bounded LLM adapters now share it.

risks.title: Retained compatibility modules may silently regain product authority
risks.signal: New documentation, CI, or features cite compatibility planning and readiness modules as the canonical MVP route.
risks.response: Keep the migration boundary machine-readable and fail the product direction gate when archived authorities reappear.

risks.title: No real end-to-end MVP vertical slice exists
risks.signal: Tree and DAG structures exist but no real project change reaches bounded execution, testing, persistence, and Agent completion judgment through the new route.
risks.response: Preserve the real Agent/worker/file-edit/pytest evidence and extend with a real-provider repair case before broader scale work.

risks.title: Deletion may outrun replacement functionality
risks.signal: Compatibility entrypoints are removed before the new DAG runtime owns equivalent execution, test, state, and result behavior.
risks.response: Enforce the cleanup boundary: migrate one vertical slice first, then delete only modules with no remaining consumer.

risks.title: Self-growth could become unrestricted self-modification
risks.signal: A discovered capability changes kernel invariants or bypasses interface, test, and registry admission.
risks.response: Limit self-growth to search, bounded trial, validated Block integration, registry admission, and measured reuse.

risks.title: Project-team features may reintroduce fixed role pipelines
risks.signal: PM, Developer, QA, Researcher, Release, or Marketing becomes a required sequential stage.
risks.response: Represent roles only as optional capability bundles/views over the same tree and DAG.

risks.title: Repository CI is not executing on the isolated branch
risks.signal: Workflow runs report startup failure with no jobs or status checks.
risks.response: Keep all verification as NOT_EVALUATED, do not merge, and obtain an executable focused verification path before promotion.

risks.title: Model-produced near-synonyms may not satisfy canonical TreeEdit fields
risks.signal: Agent output uses capability, dependencies, tool, runner, or an undeclared structural root.
risks.response: Keep machine-readable capability catalogs, strict payload validation, narrow root normalization, and fail closed before DAG execution.

risks.title: Decision efficiency is not yet better than a direct high-model call on tiny tasks
risks.signal: The one-file baseline succeeds in one high-model call while CGNK uses compose and finish checkpoints.
risks.response: Do not degrade the baseline; evaluate larger repair tasks and reduce high-model checkpoints only when evidence shows authority and recovery remain intact.

risks.title: Bounded project workers may regress adjacent generated interfaces during repair
risks.signal: A scoped repair passes action validation but replaces a declared target with code or public tests that no longer match the existing generated interfaces.
risks.response: Keep fixed budgets and external acceptance; improve public interface context, patch intent, and proposal verification before rerunning Stage 1. Never repair candidate projects manually or widen worker scope.

risks.title: Stale derived knowledge could be mistaken for current raw evidence
risks.signal: A changed or retracted leaf remains represented by an active summary returned to Conversation.
risks.response: Treat raw observations as source evidence, maintain explicit dependency edges, mark only dependent abstractions stale, exclude stale nodes from retrieval, and refresh them explicitly on demand or in a batch.

risks.title: Monolithic ProjectKnowledgePack persistence may dominate large write cost
risks.signal: Production v2 local updates passed through 250k, and the optimized derived checkpoint cold-start is 8.064 seconds versus the 37.430 second S0 baseline.
risks.response: Use v2 for new packs while retaining v1 readability, explicit migration, hash and policy validation, and authoritative replay fallback for missing or corrupt derived checkpoint data.

risks.title: Common or skewed retrieval terms produce linearly growing candidate sets
risks.signal: Exact query P50 stays near constant, but ambiguous candidate maxima reach 5,000 and P95 reaches 199.71 ms at 250k; 10k long-tail skew reaches 2,312 candidates.
risks.response: Preserve recall and retrieval authority; profile branch/term selectivity and add only semantics-preserving derived acceleration after the persistence authority is made crash-safe.

risks.title: Experimental capability growth may create registry debt instead of reusable value
risks.signal: New capabilities have zero or single reuse, repeat existing semantic signatures, or fail hidden generalization while task completion appears high.
risks.response: Keep production admission disabled; require search, bounded composition, semantic duplicate checks, hidden qualification, independent group registries, and explicit saturation/debt metrics before recommending productionization.
